pulls.author: merykitty
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi, Turns out we have never correctly computed the anti-dependence of memory access intrinsics. pulls.title: 8393488: RISC-V: Make float16ToFloat ignore upper argument bits
pulls.author: zifeihan
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi ,please consider. this patch fix the RISC-V implementation of `Float.float16ToFloat` when the incoming short argument has non-normalized upper bits. The JVM verifier represents short values as integers on the operand stack. Therefore, valid bytecode may invoke `float16ToFloat(short)` without first sign-extending the low 16 bits. The RISC-V NaN/infinity slow path previously shifted the complete source register and assumed that it was already sign-extended. pulls.title: 8393271: VectorAPI: ByteVector argument to a non-inlined method is materialized on the heap
pulls.author: vpelikh
pulls.body_excerpt: ## Problem A Vector API value passed as an argument to a method that C2 does **not** inline is materialized on the heap at the call site. The callee is compiled separately, so the value cannot stay in a SIMD register across the boundary; C2 boxes it as a vector proxy object plus its primitive array payload. A method that applies a sequence of Vector API operations (no loops, just one operation after another) is large by construction: each operation is a separate call in the bytecode, so a method with a dozen of them easily exceeds `FreqInlineSize` (325 bytes by default). pulls.title: 8388474: RISC-V: Relax satp mode check for sv57
pulls.author: zifeihan
pulls.body_excerpt: The RISC-V currently refuses to start when the kernel reports an sv57 MMU in /proc/cpuinfo, exiting during VM initialization with "Unsupported satp mode:". This is overly conservative: although sv57 hardware supports 57-bit virtual addresses, userspace never actually sees addresses beyond the sv48 range under the kernel's default address-space policy[1]. pulls.title: 8378626: C2: Move LoadNodes above loops
pulls.author: merykitty
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi, Currently, a load can only be scheduled before a loop if all of its inputs are before that loop. In this PR, we try to hoist the load above a loop even when the memory input is not a loop-invariant. To do that, we try to analyze the loop, and if all memory accesses in the loop does not interfere with the load, we rewire the memory input of the load to the memory state at the loop entry. This allows the load to be scheduled before the loop. This transformation is performed during the early placement computation of the graph, right after we have built the `IdealLoopTree`.
